title: pairtime event
description: One normalized pairtime event (docs/design/struggle-metric.md section 1, with the changes in docs/DESIGN.md section 4.1): the envelope fields, then kind, then the kind's payload under data. Go's pkg/event is the reference implementation, and its tests fail if this file and the Go types drift. This schema checks each field and each kind's rules. Go's Validate also checks the rules that compare two fields, such as typed_len_est = len_chars - pasted_chars, which this schema doesn't state. Write integers as integer literals: JSON Schema's integer accepts 1e3 and 12.0, but Go's decoder refuses them. Properties marked "x-local": true hold prompt text or hashes of private things; they never leave the device. Identifiers that stand in for something private are opaque keys keyed per device (see $defs/key). The key format rejects separators, spaces, dots and '@', so a path, a command line with arguments or an email address can't pass as one, but a bare name like Makefile can: the keying keeps a key private, not the format.

device_id.description: A random per-install id, never derived from hardware.

seq.description: The s of the device's ledger record that holds the event (docs/spec/ledger-v1.md 4.1). Ledger records are numbered from 1 with no gaps, checkpoints and upload-failure notes included, so events' seq values skip the numbers those records hold. The server uses it for exactly-once ingest. The agent assigns it when it writes the event and overwrites whatever a sender wrote.

t.description: Client wall time when the adapter saw the event.

mono.description: Monotonic clock reading in milliseconds at the same moment, so the server can re-anchor t within one boot.

boot_id.description: Linux's boot_id, or an id generated per boot elsewhere.

source.description: What the record claims produced it.

via.description: How the pairtime agent received the record. The agent sets it and overwrites whatever a sender wrote, so a sender can't choose its own.

harness_version.description: The harness's version as it reports it.

session_key.description: The harness session id salted per device, or "none" for OS and git events.

project_key.description: The client's id for the project. Absent when no project applies.

data.description: The kind's payload; see the rules in allOf.

key.description: An opaque key: 1 to 128 letters, digits, '_' or '-'. Keyed per device, as an HMAC under a device secret or a random id, never a plain hash someone could recompute from a guess.

uuid_v7.description: A UUIDv7 (RFC 9562) in canonical lowercase text form.

unix_ms.description: Unix milliseconds, UTC. The bounds (2020 to 2100) catch a time in seconds or microseconds.

git_id.description: A git object id: 40 lowercase hex digits, or 64 in a SHA-256 repository.

text64.description: One line of text: no control characters.

source.description: What the record claims produced it. cli is the AGENTS.md fallback, pairtime track.

via.description: How the agent received the record: a harness hook, a log reader, the OTLP receiver, the OS and .git watchers, a shell integration, an editor heartbeat that passed or failed the peer-process check, a WakaTime bridge record from a heartbeat that passed or failed it, pairtime track, or a plugin. macOS skips the check, so for now its editor heartbeats are editor and its bridge records bridge_unverified (docs/errata/2026-11-19-bridge-unverified.md). An anchor's evidence level depends on it, and only hook, log, otel, editor and bridge records count toward logged_s.

harness.description: other is an agent pairtime has no value for yet; none marks OS and git events.

log_match.description: matched: a log reader holds the user entry from the same session within TRACK_LOG_MATCH_S; unmatched: a reader covers the session but held no match when the call was recorded; no_reader: no reader covers the session.

env_hint.description: The name of a harness environment variable that pairtime track looks for in its caller's environment. The list is closed, so a variable's value can't pass as a name.

session.start.description: A harness session started, resumed, was cleared, compacted or forked.

automation_flags.description: The harness's own automation tells, such as background_agent.

parent_class.description: The nearest ancestor process that isn't a plain interactive shell.

permission_mode.description: As the harness names it, such as acceptEdits or on-request.

reason.description: The harness's own end reason, such as logout.

prompt.submit.description: A prompt reached the agent. Whether a person typed it is decided later, from OS evidence.

minhash.description: MinHash sketch of the normalized prompt, for re-roll detection.

error_sig.description: Hashed signature of an error pasted into the prompt.

slash_command.description: The command name only, never its arguments.

text.description: The prompt text, encrypted on the device; standard padded base64. Plain prompt text never goes in a prompt.submit event. The one event field that holds it is cli.track's label, which is local too.

agent.output.description: Output the agent showed in a turn.

words.description: Displayed assistant text only, not hidden thinking.

agent.tool.description: One tool call by the agent.

files.description: The paths the tool touched, each as an opaque key keyed per device: an HMAC under a device key, never a plain hash a reader could recompute from a guessed path. editor.activity's file_hash takes the same form, so an agent's edit and a person's edit of one file compare equal.

cmd_hash.description: Hash of the normalized command, for tools that run one.

exit_code.description: Absent for tools that don't run a process.

error_sig.description: The signature of an error in the tool's output, as an opaque key: HMAC(K_feat, signature) truncated to 16 bytes, so revealing it in tier 2 leaks nothing a guess can test.

agent.permission.description: A permission request and its answer.

agent.interrupt.description: The person stopped a running turn.

agent.queue.description: A message typed while the agent was working.

stop_hook_active.description: A stop hook made the turn continue, as /goal does.

pending_crons.description: The session's scheduled prompts at this stop. Device-only: the prefix hashes are digests of prompt text.

prefix_hash.description: Hash of the scheduled prompt's first 1,000 characters.

schedule.description: As the harness reports it, such as */20 * * * *.

editor.activity.description: An edit, save, navigation or other act in an editor, usually from a WakaTime heartbeat.

editor.description: The editor, such as vscode or neovim.

file_hash.description: The file's path as an opaque key keyed per device: an HMAC under a device key, in the same form as agent.tool's files, never a plain hash a reader could recompute from a guessed path.

shell.command.description: A command run in a shell.

exit_code.description: Absent when the source doesn't record one, as zsh and fish history files don't.

t_end.description: Not before t_start; equal to it when the run's length is unknown.

error_sig.description: The signature of an error in the command's output, as an opaque key in agent.tool's form: HMAC(K_feat, signature) truncated to 16 bytes.

git.change.description: A commit, checkout, push or other change seen in a repo's .git directory.

sha.description: The commit the operation produced or moved HEAD to.

agent_trailer.description: The agent a commit trailer credits, such as claude or aider. Never the raw trailer, which can carry a person's name and email address.

os.presence.description: One idle-time sample, taken every 15 seconds.

idle_any_s.description: Seconds since the last keyboard or mouse input.

idle_keys_s.description: Seconds since the last key press, or null where the OS can't tell keys from other input. Never less than idle_any_s, give or take a second.

app_hash.description: Per-device hash of the focused app's identity.

hosted_sessions.description: Session keys of harness processes running under the focused window's process.

focus_project.description: The project the focused window resolves to.

os.power.description: The machine suspended, resumed, locked or unlocked.

otel.active_time.description: Claude Code's own active-time metric. It calibrates the scorer and is never credit.

cli.track.description: A coding agent ran pairtime track, following the AGENTS.md entry. The model's own claim: it opens an anchor only under the four conditions of DESIGN 5.4, at level C unless keyboard input in the host window in the 10 s before the call makes it level A, and never counts toward logged_s.

label.description: The text the model passed, on one line: the user's message with personal information removed. Prompt text, so it stays on the device.

text_len.description: The number of characters the model passed. Shareable, unlike the label.

env_hints.description: The harness variables in $defs/env_hint that are set in the caller's environment, by name and never by value.

log_match.description: Whether a pairtime log reader holds the user entry the call copies.
